source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: WebSearch aggregation of investor/PLI coverage: Aurobindo subsidiary Lyfius Pharma received PLI-scheme approval to build Penicillin-G (15,000 MT) and 7-ACA (2,000 MT) capacity (committed investment ~Rs 2,205cr, incentive up to Rs 3,600cr over 6 years) explicitly framed as reducing dependence on imported Chinese key starting materials/APIs; separately, recent earnings-call commentary describes reducing third-party API dependency and building captive supply for Europe/Canada. No single AR passage explicitly attributes revenue growth to 'China+1', hence moderate rather than strong.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Uses forward contracts and options to hedge foreign-currency exposure (third-party analyst commentary); no specific hedge ratio or policy text located in primary AR (site blocked in this environment).
inr_exposure.evidence: Third-party analysis (unverified against primary AR): Aurobindo earns over 70% of consolidated revenue in USD and EUR combined while reporting in INR; FY25 geography split reported in market coverage as US ~Rs 14,816cr, Europe ~Rs 10,315cr, Growth Markets ~Rs 3,499cr against total revenue of ~Rs 31,724cr (i.e. these three together ~90% of revenue).

pli_scheme.evidence: Government/press coverage: Aurobindo (via Lyfius Pharma) approved under the Bulk Drugs PLI scheme for Penicillin-G and 7-ACA production, commercial production targeted from FY24 with incentive payouts through FY29-30; specific % of company revenue attributable to PLI-linked output not disclosed in sources reviewed.

ABB.report_year: CY2024 (ABB India reports on a Jan-Dec fiscal year)

china_plus_one.evidence: Q4 CY2024 earnings-call coverage (Yahoo Finance/Business Standard summaries): exports are ~10% of ABB India's revenue mix under a stated 'local for local' domestic strategy; one earnings summary notes 'growth in export markets within the Distribution Solutions division' but with no China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing or explicit revenue attribution.

govt_capex.evidence: News center/earnings coverage: management cites sustained public capex in infrastructure, railways and green energy as a demand driver; ABB secured a Mumbai Metro traction/propulsion systems contract via its Titagarh Rail Systems partnership (metro/rail entry) and cites a strong order pipeline across power, metro, renewables, railways, T&D and data centres. No revenue % attributed to government/PLI-linked capex specifically.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (foreign-currency revenue exposure) reported at ~10% of total revenue in Q4 CY2024 earnings coverage; no hedging policy details located (ABB India IR site, NSE archives, and Scribd copy of the Integrated AR 2024 were all unreachable in this environment).

rural.evidence: Third-party market coverage (2024): United Spirits' 'extensive pan-India distribution network offers reach across urban and rural markets' and management/analyst commentary expects Tier-2/3/4 and rural consumption growth to outpace urban; no specific rural revenue % disclosed in sources reviewed (primary AR host nsearchives.nseindia.com and media.diageo.com were unreachable in this environment).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party FY24 analysis (Equitymaster-style summary): debt-to-equity ~0.0x in both FY23 and FY24, interest coverage improved to 25.4x (from 13.3x), indicating minimal net debt; no floating-rate liability % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Industry/press commentary: extra neutral alcohol (ENA) and glass together are cited as roughly half of USL's raw material cost base; glass/PET packaging carries indirect petrochemical-linked cost exposure, but no AR-disclosed % tied specifically to crude oil was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26 earnings commentary and broker notes (Investing.com, ICICI Direct, Oct 2025-Jan 2026): Navin Fluorine described as 'well placed for margin stability and China Plus One tailwind'; company has signed long-term fluorspar supply contracts with South African miners to reduce dependence on China-controlled fluorspar supply, and reports growing European CDMO traction and new long-term specialty-molecule supply contracts. No confirmed direct AR quote explicitly attributing revenue growth to China+1 was located.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Analyst/rating reports (FY25): consolidated debt rose from ₹1,368 crore (FY24) to ₹1,466 crore (FY25), largely term debt funding Dahej/Surat capex; net debt/PBILDT improved to 1.79x from 2.14x. Floating vs fixed-rate split not disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Q2 FY26 earnings commentary: raw material costs rose 39.7% YoY to Rs 312.9 crore; key inputs are fluorspar (globally China-concentrated supply) and HFC/petrochemical derivatives. Exact % of raw materials linked to crude/petrochemical prices not disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Q4 FY25 result update (Business Standard/broker notes): export contribution ~77% of quarterly revenue, indicating significant foreign-currency revenue exposure. Specific hedging policy not disclosed in sources reviewed.

MEDANTA.report_year: FY2022-23 (most recent verified geography split; later FY24-26 figures only partially available)

rural.evidence: FY2023 investor presentation (read directly, dated May 2023): Medanta's network (Gurgaon, Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi, Indore, plus under-construction Noida) is described as covering 'over 400 million people' across catchment states, but hospitals are sited in metro/Tier-1 and state-capital locations, not framed as rural-focused. FY25 expansion pipeline (Mumbai, Pitampura/South Delhi, Guwahati) is likewise metro-oriented. No explicit rural revenue % is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY2023 investor presentation (read directly): company moved to a net cash position (₹4,692 million net cash) as of March 2023 after IPO proceeds were used to repay debt; gross debt was ₹8,422 million. Floating vs fixed-rate split not disclosed. FY25 broker notes indicate fresh debt-funded capex (~₹3,500 crore for a 3,000-bed expansion plan) is underway; updated debt mix not verified in this pass.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY2023 investor presentation (read directly): international patient revenue was 6% of total revenue in FY23 (up from 4% in FY22), growing 68% YoY to INR 1,564 million. Q1 FY26 update (AlphaStreet transcript, search snippet): international patient revenue grew 34% YoY to Rs 636 million, but full-year FY25 % of total revenue was not found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: FY25 results commentary (search snippets, press releases): domestic revenue grew 16.4% YoY, supported by a network of C&F agents and 5,000+ field personnel; no rural-specific revenue % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 results (press release/search snippets): international revenue of ~₹4,236 crore (54% of ₹7,902 crore total revenue) is split across Emerging Markets (₹1,510cr, ~19%), Europe (₹1,474cr, ~19%), and Canada (₹1,252cr, ~16%) — i.e., predominantly EUR/CAD/other currencies rather than USD; company is separately reported to have 'minimal exposure to the US market' (US business historically routed via related party Avet Lifesciences). Specific hedging policy not disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Industry/news search snippets: Emcure Pharmaceuticals is named as one of nine domestic pharmaceutical companies approved under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Group B - complex generics/biologics category). Revenue % attributable to PLI-incentivized production not disclosed in sources reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: FY25 company/press commentary (AlCircle, BigMint, Business Standard): India aluminium demand described as driven by infrastructure, construction and power-sector capex; India projected to become the third-largest global building & construction (B&C) aluminium market by FY33, with domestic demand seen rising from ~350kt to ~719kt over the next decade. Hindalco announced ~₹50,000 crore India investment over 3 years and a $10bn five-year global growth plan. Exact % of revenue attributable specifically to government capex not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY25 press commentary: capex of ₹18,000 crore in FY25 (highest in nearly a decade), part of a $10bn five-year investment program, implies continued reliance on debt funding; specific floating-rate debt % not disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: FY25 results commentary: record Aluminium Upstream EBITDA (₹4,838 crore, +79% YoY) was attributed in part to 'lower input costs' (coal and alumina); crude-oil-linked inputs (fuel oil, pitch/CPC, caustic soda) are a known cost driver in aluminium smelting, but the exact % of raw material costs linked to crude/petrochemical prices was not disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Novelis (Hindalco's wholly-owned subsidiary) FY25 10-K segment data (SEC filings, via search): third-party sales by region were North America $7,030mn (~25% of Hindalco consolidated FY25 revenue of $27.86bn), Europe $4,575mn (~16%), South America $2,624mn (~9%), Asia $2,492mn (~9%) — Novelis in total ~60% of consolidated revenue, all LME/USD-linked. Analyst reports separately indicate ~7% of Hindalco's domestic (India) aluminium volumes were hedged at ~US$2,900/tonne in FY24 (most recent disclosed data point found); FY25-specific hedged % not located.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel (₹6,322 crore outlay, launched 2021) is steel-sector specific; search results on scheme beneficiaries do not name Hindalco (an aluminium/copper producer), indicating the scheme is not applicable to Hindalco's core businesses.

govt_capex.evidence: Company profile / search summaries: Netweb supplies HPC, supercomputing, private cloud and AI systems to hyper-scale, enterprise and government data centers, including government/defense-linked HPC deployments; no specific revenue % from government capex disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: IIFL 4QFY25 result review / Netweb 3QFY25 investor update (via search): export business ~5-9% of total revenue in FY25 (sales to Middle East, Europe, USA), expected to reach ~10-11% medium-term; implies ~93% domestic/INR revenue. Figures are from analyst/IR update snippets, not directly read from the AR PDF.

pli_scheme.evidence: EquityBulls press release (via search): Netweb Technologies India Ltd received its first incentive claim under PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware, amounting to Rs 5.94 crore for the period July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024. Revenue % contribution from PLI not disclosed.

rural.evidence: Company strategy commentary (via search, not primary AR MD&A text): Titan is aggressively expanding into Tier 2/3/4 towns (400,000+ sq ft added annually; 3,603 stores across 440+ towns by FY25-26) citing rising disposable incomes and under-penetration as growth drivers; no specific rural/semi-urban revenue % disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Gold procurement hedging (advance contracts, gold-on-lease with banks) providing multi-month supply/price visibility; not a revenue-side FX hedging policy per se.
inr_exposure.evidence: CFO commentary (via search): Titan has secured ~120-day gold supply visibility through advance procurement contracts and hedging mechanisms to manage gold price/import risk. International footprint (Tanishq/Mia/CaratLane, ~23-32 stores in US/GCC) is growing (North America +85% YoY, GCC ~38% YoY per recent quarters) but remains a small share of total revenue; exact international revenue % not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/strategy summaries (via search, not directly confirmed from AR MD&A text): Bharat Forge is adding forging/machining capacity in the US and Europe to serve OEMs locally and capture share amid 'China Plus One' supply-chain diversification; company is shifting mix from ICE-auto toward defense/aerospace/industrial, targeting non-auto revenue >50% of consolidated revenue by 2027 (from ~40% in 2023). Explicit AR-text attribution of revenue/order growth specifically to China+1 was not directly verified (source PDFs unreachable in this environment), hence graded 'moderate' rather than 'strong'.

govt_capex.evidence: Business Standard / company commentary (via search): Bharat Forge defense revenue grew from ~Rs 410 crore (FY23) to ~Rs 1,772 crore (FY25), against consolidated FY25 revenue of ~Rs 15,123 crore (Rs 151,228 million) — implying defense/government-linked revenue of roughly 12% of consolidated revenue. This is a derived estimate combining two separately disclosed absolute figures, not a single stated percentage from the AR; defense order backlog cited at >Rs 5,000 crore by mid-2025.

rate_sensitive.evidence: CARE Ratings / analyst commentary (via search): net debt/EBITDA ~1.1x in FY2024; Q1FY26 finance costs down 33.5% YoY to Rs 82.22 crore. Specific % of liabilities on floating-rate terms not disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: PESTLE/analyst summaries (via search): raw materials (mainly steel/HRC) represent an estimated 25-30% of costs, with HRC steel price volatility flagged as a risk; INR depreciation cited as raising import costs for technology/inputs by an estimated 2-3pp of COGS. This is steel/metal commodity exposure rather than direct crude-oil-linked raw material; no crude-oil-specific % disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Forex hedges covering an estimated ~45% of anticipated FX exposure (2024), supplemented by natural hedging from manufacturing operations in Germany, UK and US.
inr_exposure.evidence: Investor presentation (Feb 2025 Q3FY25 update, via search): export business accounts for ~30% of consolidated FY25 revenue. Analyst commentary: forex hedges cover ~45% of anticipated FX exposure (2024) plus natural hedges from overseas manufacturing (Germany, UK, US).

pli_scheme.evidence: Ministry of Heavy Industries PLI Auto Scheme approved-beneficiary list (via search): Bharat Forge is listed as a 'Component Champion' beneficiary under the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components (Advanced Automotive Technology products), with incentive rates up to 18%. Company-specific revenue or incentive-amount impact not disclosed in sources reviewed.

NESTLEIND.report_year: FY2024-25 (transition to April-March year end; period ended March 31, 2025)

rural.evidence: Business Standard (via search, dated reporting): rural India accounted for ~25% of Nestle India's domestic revenue as of Q4 2020 (not current-year AR data). More recent commentary: company runs a 'RUrban' rural/semi-urban expansion program, adding ~5.2 lakh outlets since April 2023 and reaching ~45,300 villages by FY25-26; current fiscal-year rural revenue % not disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Business Standard commodity-cost commentary (via search): key raw materials include edible/palm oil, coffee, milk and cocoa, with milk price inflation and palm oil price swings flagged as margin drivers in recent quarters; no crude-oil/petrochemical-specific raw-material % disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Business Standard (via search): export revenue grew ~16% YoY (driven by foods, coffee, instant tea, breakfast cereals) in one period cited, while Q4FY25 export sales were reported at Rs 212.66 crore, down 8.65% YoY in another. Exports appear to be a small (likely low-single-digit) share of total revenue, but exact annual % and any hedging policy were not found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Business Standard/press coverage FY24-25: analysts note Eicher Motors' two-wheeler volume growth linked to improved rural demand and financing availability; no revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Press/analyst commentary FY24-25: cites carbon black (+~25%) and synthetic rubber (~40% peak) cost inflation and natural rubber price pressure as procurement headwinds; no raw-material % tied to crude specifically disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Press coverage (ackodrive.com, FY25): Royal Enfield motorcycle exports rose 29.7% to 100,136 units, ~10.6% of RE's total motorcycle unit sales, across 60+ countries — this is a unit/volume share of the motorcycle segment only, not a consolidated revenue export %, so not populated as a company-wide figure.

pli_scheme.evidence: PIB/Ministry of Heavy Industries PLI-Auto scheme coverage: Eicher Motors Limited listed as approved under the 'Champion OEM Incentive' scheme of the Auto PLI (disbursals starting FY2024-25 per Autocar Professional); revenue contribution % not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party equity/industry commentary (tradebrains.in, mnclgroup.com, FY24-26 coverage): export order growth from Europe, Middle East, Turkey, US and CIS attributed to a 'China+1' supply-chain shift, with TDPS positioned as a non-Chinese alternative supplier; framing is from analyst/press sources, not a directly-verified AR quote, so treated as moderate rather than strong.

inr_exposure.evidence: Press/analyst coverage of FY24-25 results: export business (incl. deemed exports) contributed ~67-68% of order inflow for FY25, with growth from US AI-data-centre gas turbine orders, Turkey geothermal, Nepal hydro, and Germany/US/CIS traction; figure is order-inflow share, used as a proxy for revenue export exposure since no revenue-specific % was found. Hedging policy not disclosed in sources reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IPO documentation (May 2025, business-standard.com/groww.in coverage): consolidated borrowings of ~INR 29,044.92 million as of 31 March 2025; ~60% (INR 16,181.27 million) earmarked for prepayment from IPO proceeds, expected to save ~INR 150 crore/year in interest costs. Floating-vs-fixed split not disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: ICICI Direct quarterly results note (FY24-25 period): exports contributed ~5.8% of Belrise Industries' manufacturing revenue; export footprint spans US, Japan, UK, China, with 250+ components single-sourced to JLR's Austria/Slovakia/UK plants in FY25. Figure is from a quarterly note, full-year AR figure not independently confirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: India Briefing/EVreporter published lists of the ~75 companies approved under the Auto PLI Component Champion Incentive Scheme (incl. Motherson Sumi, Bosch, Lucas-TVS, Tata Autocomp) do not list Belrise Industries; treated as non-beneficiary absent contrary evidence.

rural.evidence: Press/investor coverage (business-standard.com, Q1 FY26-27 materials): revenue from Tier-3+ cities cited as growing at a 16.7% CAGR from FY23 to reach ~INR 1,090 crore; company also runs a rural outreach program across seven states (110,000+ patients tested). Figure given in absolute INR, not as a % of total revenue, so left null rather than estimated.

govt_capex.evidence: Investing.com Q1 FY26 earnings coverage: management cited pricing/volume gains partly aided by government health schemes (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, ABHIM); no revenue % attributed to government-scheme business specifically.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company profile sources (GlobalData, ZoomInfo, lalpathlabsnp.com): international operations exist via subsidiaries/franchises in Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and a Dubai entity; no international/domestic revenue split % found.

rural.evidence: Business Standard coverage of Pidilite FY25 results/MD&A commentary: rural consumer sentiment described as weak versus urban in FY25, with rural markets expected to recover on a good monsoon; no rural revenue percentage disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Business Standard (Q4 FY25 / FY25 commentary): Pidilite's raw material basket is heavily weighted toward VAM (vinyl acetate monomer) and other crude-oil derivatives; weighted-average raw material costs rose ~40-50% amid West Asia geopolitical tensions, squeezing gross margins in Q4 FY25. Specific % of COGS from crude-linked inputs not disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Directors' Report / FY24-25 results summary (via India Infoline / press coverage): exports of INR 14,054 million were ~8.3% of total sales of Rs 18,087 crore in FY2024-25; ~69% of exported products (i.e. ~5.7% of total revenue) went to Robert Bosch, Germany, as intra-group transactions from the Power Solutions and Mobility Aftermarket divisions. These are largely intra-group flows rather than third-party export sales; no formal hedging policy percentage disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analysis/earnings commentary (secondary sources, not verbatim AR MD&A text confirmed): management cites the global 'China Plus One' supply-chain diversification trend as a driver of new early-phase/clinical manufacturing orders from global pharma clients, but explicit AR MD&A language with quantified revenue attribution was not located in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source commentary (equity analysis pieces referencing DRHP/AR data): exports account for ~99% of total revenue, primarily from the US and Europe (regulated markets); this implies high foreign-currency exposure, but a specific USD-denominated revenue % and hedging policy could not be confirmed from sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY25 results commentary / industry analysis (secondary sources, not verbatim AR MD&A quote confirmed): Divi's diversified geographic customer and raw-material sourcing base is cited as reducing exposure to China-linked energy-cost and supply-chain disruptions, and industry commentary frames Divi's as a beneficiary of the broader China+1 diversification trend among global pharma customers; explicit AR MD&A 'China+1' framing with quantified revenue/order attribution not located.

crude_exposure.evidence: FY25/FY26 results commentary (secondary sources): elevated solvent and raw-material costs linked to petrochemical inputs, West Asia geopolitical tensions, and China energy-cost inflation cited as pressuring input costs; company noted its diversified geography and long-term customer contracts (with built-in price pass-through mechanisms) partly mitigate this. No specific % of raw material cost from crude-linked inputs disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 results commentary (indiacsr.in and related coverage): exports were ~88% of FY25 revenue (Rs 9,712 cr total), with Europe ~56.5% and North America ~16.2% of revenue, implying substantial USD/EUR revenue exposure. Company noted forex gains/losses in recent quarters (e.g. Q3 FY26 forex gain of Rs 19 cr consolidated) but a specific hedging policy or USD-only revenue % was not confirmed in sources reviewed.
